Description:
Two NURBS cylinders whose axes cross at a right angle, with DIFFERENT radii - and that is the whole
point. EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam and its NURBS twin NurbsCylindersTangentAtSeam build the same
arrangement with EQUAL radii, and then the two mantles touch tangentially at (+-r, 0, 0) and the
intersection curve has a node there. Different radii remove exactly that and nothing else: both bodies
are still extrusions of exact nine pole NURBS circles, the axes still meet at the origin at a right
angle, the seams still lie where they lay - only the contact is gone.

  cylZ   r = 10 about the z axis, z from -20 to 30, seam on x = 10, y = 0
  cylY   r = 12 about the y axis, y from -20 to 25, seam on x = 12, z = 0

Why there can be no contact: the two cylinders are canal surfaces with spines the two axes and constant
radii 10 and 12. A common normal has to be perpendicular to both spines, which leaves n = +-x, and the
line of centres of the two touching spheres has to be parallel to it. With the axes crossing at the
origin the centres are (0,0,s) and (0,t,0), whose difference is never parallel to x unless both are the
origin - and then the two spheres are concentric with radii 10 and 12 and do not touch. So this case has
a perfectly regular intersection curve, and it is the reference for what the SAME construction does when
nothing is degenerate.

The lengths are of different and asymmetric extent (z from -20 to 30, y from -20 to 25) for the reason
EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam gives: with symmetric cylinders the two halves a difference falls into are
congruent, the canonical order of the parts of a multi solid result is then not determined, and the
recorded extents flip from run to run.
Expected:
Two closed solids and four closed results.

  cylZ   V = pi*10^2*50 = 15707.9632679490, A = 2*pi*10*50 + 2*pi*100 = 3769.9111843078,
         extent -10, -10, -20 .. 10, 10, 30
  cylY   V = pi*12^2*45 = 20357.5203952619, A = 2*pi*12*45 + 2*pi*144 = 4297.6987501108,
         extent -12, -20, -12 .. 12, 25, 12

The intersection of two crossing cylinders of different radii has no elementary closed form. For a
fixed x its cross section is the rectangle |y| <= sqrt(100-x^2), |z| <= sqrt(144-x^2), so

  V = integral from -10 to 10 of 4*sqrt((100-x^2)*(144-x^2)) dx

which is an elliptic integral. Evaluated with the substitution x = 10*sin(t), which removes the square
root endpoints, by composite Simpson, stationary to twelve digits over a sixteenfold refinement:

  crossInter   6810.025016874

and from it, exactly:
  crossUnion     15707.9632679490 + 20357.5203952619 - 6810.0250169 = 29255.4586463
  crossZminusY   15707.9632679490 - 6810.0250169 =  8897.9382511
  crossYminusZ   20357.5203952619 - 6810.0250169 = 13547.4953784

The SHAPES differ, and asymmetrically, which is the part worth checking:
  crossZminusY   TWO solids. The wider cylinder removes |z| <= sqrt(144-x^2) from every point of the
                 thinner one's disc, and that is at least sqrt(44) = 6.63 everywhere, so the thin
                 cylinder is cut clean through. The two parts are
                   pi*100*20 - crossInter/2 = 2878.1727987 and pi*100*30 - crossInter/2 = 6019.7654523
                 and they do NOT touch each other anywhere.
  crossYminusZ   ONE solid, and one with a hole: the thin cylinder cuts a slot right through the wide
                 one, open on both mantle sides, so what is left hangs together only around the slot.
                 Euler 0 rather than 2 is what to expect here.

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS - HISTORICAL, THE DEFECT IS FIXED. A planar face whose outline is a
rational NURBS circle used to be measured through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea ->
GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for most radii that biarc approximation
degenerated into four straight lines, so the lid measured 2*r*r instead of pi*r*r. It was not even a
threshold: exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5,
6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25. Every radius in this case was therefore taken from the first list, so
that its numbers would be the geometry and not a measurement artefact.
Since 2026-09-21 BSpline2D integrates the swept area of a rational spline instead of approximating it
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and every radius is exact. The radii here are left as they are -
they cost nothing and the case does not need rewriting - but a new case no longer has to avoid any.
Status:
Green from the day it was written, 2026-09-17, and stable over 3 repeats. It is the contact free
reference for NurbsCylindersTangentAtSeam: the same construction with the same seams, only the radii
differ, and with different radii the two mantles cannot touch. All four operations return, crossZminusY
falls into the two predicted parts and crossYminusZ has Euler 0, the slot cut through the wider
cylinder.

TWO VALUES ARE NOT FULLY EXPLAINED and are deliberately NOT marked verified:
  crossUnion     29259.6012503 against the derived 29255.4586463   1.4e-4 HIGH
  crossYminusZ   13551.0949016 against the derived 13547.4953784   2.7e-4 HIGH
while everything around them is far better: crossInter is 7.0e-6 from its quadrature value and the two
parts of crossZminusY are within 1.5e-5 of theirs. The identity union + intersection = cylZ + cylY is
therefore met only to 1.1e-4, and the sign is the suspicious part - a volume summed over a triangulation
of a curved body normally comes out LOW, as crossInter does. The deviation is systematic, identical over
three repeats, so it is not scatter. Both affected bodies are the ones that carry a large trimmed
SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion face; whether that is a measurement defect there or a real excess of material
is open. It is small enough not to hold the case back and large enough to be worth a look.

crossInter.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 6809.9772993 against 6810.02501687, 7.0e-06. against the quadrature value given in Expected. Four SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion faces and no lid: the body stays clear of both pairs of caps, as it must.

crossZminusY#0.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 6019.81396645 against 6019.76545233, 8.1e-06. the upper part. Its lower extent 6.63324958071 is exactly sqrt(44) = sqrt(144-100), the smallest half thickness of the slab the wide cylinder removes - so the cut is where it belongs.

crossZminusY#1.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 2878.21280417 against 2878.17279874, 1.4e-05. the lower part, upper extent -sqrt(44) by the same argument.

cylZ.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 15707.9632292 against 15707.9632679, 2.5e-09. two SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion faces and two lids, edgeLength exactly the predicted 2*4*10*sqrt(2) + 2*50.
